d.title: Execution failed, or the answer is bad
d.caption: **The split is correct and it needs a convention.** “I could not run your tool” and “I ran it and there is no rate for XXX” are genuinely different facts, and collapsing them would lose information — a missing rate is not a malfunction. But it means **the semantic error channel is yours to define and the protocol will not help you be consistent.** Pick one shape for the whole server, document it in the instructions, and use it everywhere: a server where half the tools return an error key and the other half a status key is one a model handles badly for no reason.

d.title: Three things the decorators never made you write
d.caption: **Two handlers replace a decorator per tool:** one returning the tool list, one dispatching a call by name. The cost is visible in every row — the `inputSchema` as a literal dictionary, the `if name != ...` branch, and the whole of `InitializationOptions`, which is the object FastMCP had been assembling silently all along. **Writing it once is what makes the handshake in lesson 1.2 stop being something that happens and start being something you chose.**
